title: Smith
dek: Refine materials and recover resources from magic items.
body:
← Crafting & Skill Experience

Smiths serve an important role in the magic item economy of Fenumion. They specialize in the many processes that encompass the transmutation of materials and finished products. Smiths can refine Materials gathered by scouts into higher-rarity versions, as well as break down magic items into their component materials or even costly spell components.

The Smith Progression Table

Smith · table 1
Skill LevelSkill Exp. RequiredAbilities
Apprentice1,000Convert 1d4 Common Materials to 1 Uncommon Material
+2 to Refining Rolls
Break down Uncommon items into spell components
Journeyman4,000Convert 1d2 Common Materials to 1 Uncommon Material
Convert 1d4 Uncommon Materials into 1 Rare Material
+4 to Refining Rolls
Break down Rare non-attunement items into spell components
Expert10,000Convert 1d2 Uncommon Materials to 1 Rare Material
Convert 1d4 Rare Materials into 1 Very Rare Material
+6 to Refining Rolls
Break down Rare attunement items into spell components
Master20,000Convert 1d2 Rare Materials to 1 Very Rare Material
Convert 1d4 Very Rare Materials into 1 Legendary Material
+8 to Refining Rolls
Break down Very Rare items into spell components

How it Works

To refine, the smith rolls a d20 and adds to it their proficiency bonus and their skill level modifier. Another smith of the same skill level or higher may use the Help action to give advantage on that roll. The Artificer class feature Magic Item Adept/Savant/Master confers an additional bonus to the refining roll of +1, +2, or +3, depending on the highest level of this feature for that Artificer. This roll cannot be modified in any way except as outlined in this skill description. The difficulty for refining materials varies based on the rarity as defined below:

Common to Uncommon: DC 9

Uncommon to Rare: DC 15

Rare to Very Rare: DC 21

Very Rare to Legendary: DC 27

Refining materials is an imperfect process, so each time the smith makes a refinement roll, they roll a 1d4 or 1d2 as determined in the Abilities column of the table above to see how many materials are consumed in the refinement.

If the refinement roll fails to meet the DC, one material is destroyed as part of the process. Should the refinement roll fail by 10 or more, half of the materials are destroyed as part of the failure (minimum of 1 material destroyed). A roll of a natural 1 destroys all materials. Should a smith fail two consecutive refinement rolls, they must wait 24 hours before they may attempt another refinement.

Smiths can also reclaim materials from magic items by breaking them down in one of two ways: either for parts or into costly spell components. If breaking down items for parts, they will only receive scouted materials, not hunter components.

Breaking Down Items for Parts

Smith · table 2
Journeyman Smith50% of materials, rounded down
Exper Smith75% of materials, rounded down
Master Smith100% of materials

Breaking Down Items for Spell Components

Smith · table 3
Apprentice SmithDismantle an uncommon item into 1d4 spell components worth 100gp or less, but not worth more in total than the item’s cost in the shop document. No diamonds or delerium.
Journeyman SmithDismantle a rare non-attunement item into 1d4 spell components worth 500gp or less, but not worth more in total than the item’s cost in the shop document. No diamonds or delerium.
Expert SmithDismantle a rare attunement item into 1d4 spell components worth 1000gp or less, but not worth more in total than the item’s cost in the shop document. No diamonds or delerium.
Master SmithDismantle a very rare item into 1d4 spell components worth 2500gp or less, but not worth more in total than the item’s cost in the shop document. No diamonds or delerium.
